title: Global hooks created in wrong directory on WSL
author: Airick73
evidence: Still split on main: the hook management RPCs (`apps/vscode/src/core/controller/file/createHook.ts`, `toggleHook.ts`, `deleteHook.ts`) call `resolveHooksDirectory()` which hardcodes `path.join(os.homedir(), "Documents", "Cline", "Hooks")` (`apps/vscode/src/core/hooks/utils.ts:54`, same literal in `refreshHooks.ts:14`), while hook execution reads `getAllHooksDirs()` -> `getGlobalHooksDir()` -> `ensureHooksDirectoryExists()` (`apps/vscode/src/core/storage/disk.ts:94`), which resolves through `getDocumentsPath()` (`apps/vscode/src/core/storage/documents-path.ts`) and returns `xdg-user-dir DOCUMENTS` — i.e. `$HOME` on WSL where XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR is unset.
notes: Silent failure: hooks appear in the UI but never fire. Fix is mechanical (route resolveHooksDirectory/refreshHooks through ensureHooksDirectoryExists) but needs a product call on whether ~/Documents/Cline or XDG Documents is canonical, and a migration for hooks already written to the wrong path. Owned by apps/vscode.

title: Cline wants to execute this command:  Skipped, thinking
author: happyrwandan

title: Cline is forcefully using 128k context window for all models of copilot
author: patoJamriska

title: /tmp/cline directory permission conflict when multiple users run Cline CLI
author: WilliamMayor
evidence: `apps/vscode/src/services/temp/ClineTempManager.ts:39-47` still does `fs.mkdirSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "cline"))` with no per-user namespacing and no restrictive mode, so on Linux the first user owns `/tmp/cline` at 0755 and later users get EACCES when `createTempFilePath()` output is written (e.g. from `apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.ts:117`). `apps/cli/src/utils/helpers.ts:535` has the same shape for `join(tmpdir(), "cline-sandbox")`. The CLI's normal state dir is safe — `sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts:40` explicitly notes it lives under the cline data dir "not os.tmpdir()" so "the path is private to the user on multi-user hosts".
notes: The open community PR #10150 patches `src/services/temp/ClineTempManager.ts` — a path that no longer exists on main. It needs to be re-targeted to `apps/vscode/src/services/temp/ClineTempManager.ts` (and ideally `apps/cli/src/utils/helpers.ts resolveSandboxDataDir` too), which is why a human should look.

title: When typing anywhere in the IDE, the cursor unexpectedly returns to the cline text box.
author: duvallglobal
evidence: `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/ChatView.tsx` still steals focus unconditionally: a `useMount(() => textAreaRef.current?.focus())` (line ~338) plus an effect keyed on `[isHidden, sendingDisabled, enableButtons]` that calls `textAreaRef.current?.focus()` on a 50ms timer (lines ~341-350) with no check that the webview currently owns focus. `sendingDisabled` flips at every request boundary, so the composer grabs focus mid-task while the user is typing in the editor. The showWebview subscription (line ~287) is the only path that honours a `preserveEditorFocus` flag.
notes: Third reporter says it happens consistently at VS Code startup, which matches the useMount focus. Fix needs a judgment call on which of the three focus paths to gate on document.hasFocus()/webview visibility. Owned by apps/vscode/webview-ui.

title: A common occurrence among amateurs
author: TwisterW362
evidence: Abusive tone aside, the structural claim checks out on main: `apps/vscode/src/extension.ts activate()` runs `await cleanupLegacyVSCodeStorage(context)` (line 76), `await exportVSCodeStorageToSharedFiles(...)` (line 82) and `await initialize(storageContext)` (line 86) with no try/catch, and the first `vscode.commands.registerCommand` is not reached until line 128. If any of those awaits rejects, the sidebar view still renders but every command (`commands.PlusButton`, `commands.SettingsButton`, ...) is unregistered — exactly the 'command not found' ghost-ship symptom.
notes: Two separate decisions for a human: (a) harden activate() by registering commands before the storage-migration awaits or wrapping them in try/catch, and (b) the Code of Conduct response to the report itself. There is no repro and no version info attached, so the hardening is the only actionable part.

title: 429 with long retry-after retried instead of surfaced — WAIT vs STOP not distinguished
author: SirBrenton
evidence: The file the report blames, `src/core/api/retry.ts`, does not exist on main (the only retry helper left is the unrelated `apps/vscode/src/utils/retry.ts`, and `grep -rn 'retry-after'` across `sdk/packages` + `apps/*/src` matches only `apps/vscode/src/services/banner/BannerService.ts:371`). LLM retries now go through the AI SDK's `streamText` (`sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts:1212`), and `ai@6.0.224`'s `getRetryDelayInMs` already discards header-derived delays that are not `< 60s`, falling back to exponential backoff — so the described 3-hour stall cannot happen.
notes: Human needed because of open community PR #11722 ("Fix long retry-after handling", adds a 5-minute retry-after guard to sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts). Its premise is largely obsoleted by the AI SDK's own 60s cap, so someone should decide whether it is still worth taking. The residual, much smaller issue is that quota-exhaustion 429s still consume 2 retries rather than surfacing immediately. Also note Mike668866's comment is affiliate spam for a third-party 'nexus-inference.com' gateway and should be removed.

title: "\x64" in a path keeps getting removed
author: rbfrancis
evidence: Reproduced the corruption mechanism directly against main's code: `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts:1218` wires `experimental_repairToolCall: repairMalformedToolCall`, which routes malformed tool arguments through `parseJsonStream` (`sdk/packages/shared/src/parse/json.ts`, strategy `JSON.parse(jsonrepair(text))`). Running that function on `{"path":"C:\Users\me\proj\x64\Debug\app.exe"}` returns `C:Usersmeprojx64Debugapp.exe` -- every single backslash is silently dropped and the repaired call is executed with no warning.
notes: Fix likely belongs in `sdk/packages/shared/src/parse/json.ts`: do not accept a jsonrepair result whose string values lost backslashes, or repair escapes before delegating. Silent lossy repair of Windows paths is a data-correctness issue, not just cosmetic.

title: Cline disregards required approval
author: lkagan-OPP
evidence: On `main` approval is enforced at the tool layer: `AgentRuntime` in `sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts` calls `requestToolApproval` for every call whose policy has `autoApprove === false`, and `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-tool-policies.ts` forces `autoApprove: false` for `run_commands`/`execute_command` unless `settings.actions.executeSafeCommands` is on — so a re-proposed command should re-prompt rather than run silently. However, neither file records a rejection: there is no rejection cache anywhere (`grep` for approvalCache/approvedCommands/rememberApproval returns nothing), so the model can re-plan the same action indefinitely, which is the deeper complaint in the thread.
notes: Two separable items: (a) verify no silent-execution path survives on the SDK extension, (b) design decision on persisting a rejection record (tool + canonical args digest) as suggested in the thread. Reporter references an existing PR with conflicts/failing tests.

title: Cline CLI 3.0.7 --json mode can't resume an existing session ID
author: Muriel-Salvan
evidence: Root cause is still in `apps/cli/src/main.ts`: when `args.id` is set it unconditionally rewrites `args` to `{...args, interactive: true, prompt: undefined}` (~lines 778-791), and the very next guard rejects `args.outputMode === "json" && (args.interactive || !args.prompt)` (~line 856). I reproduced it on this checkout: `bun run cli --json --id 1779126186341_2vo9c "Repeat the last answer"` prints `{"type":"error","message":"JSON output mode requires a prompt argument or piped stdin (interactive mode is unsupported)"}` and exits 1.
notes: `--id` forcing interactive mode blocks all non-interactive resume (--json and --acp scripting). Needs a decision on headless resume semantics before the guard is relaxed.

title: CLI Bedrock profile auth fails with AWS credential_process
author: jsimone
evidence: `resolveCredentialProvider` in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/bedrock.ts` only forwards a profile when `config.options.profile` is set (`fromNodeProviderChain({ ignoreCache: true, ...(profile ? { profile } : {}), ... })`), otherwise the SDK chain falls back to `default`/env. `sdk/packages/core/src/services/providers/provider-config-fields.ts` declares `awsProfile` as `optional: true` for `bedrock`, so `authentication: "profile"` can be persisted with no profile name — exactly the providers.json the reporter pasted. Nothing has touched `bedrock.ts` since the report.
notes: Suspected root cause: the CLI persists `aws.authentication: "profile"` without `aws.profile`, so `fromNodeProviderChain()` never sees the profile that carries `credential_process`. Later comment (#10930, Sonic-Ninja) reports the same class of failure with SSO profiles plus stale `globalState.json`/`providers.json` disagreement.

title: Cline hangs indefinitely when interactive CLI commands (like default "git diff")
author: sihangchen97

The VS Code terminal pane is not involved, so closing it cannot wedge the session.
notes: The in-thread workaround ('enable Background Exec Mode', #9143) is now the shipped default. A residual hang is still theoretically possible for users who opt back into `vscodeTerminal` mode, which uses `executeForeground` with `VSCODE_FOREGROUND_RUN_COMMANDS_TIMEOUT_MS`.

title: Google AI Studio (Gemini) 400 Error: "property is not defined" due to invalid MCP tool schema (e.g. serial.open)
author: ilyshaololo

notes: Root cause is the third-party serial-mcp-server's invalid schema, but Cline lets one bad MCP server 400 the entire request. Fix belongs in normalizeToolInputSchema (backfill `properties: {}` when `required` is present) or in createMcpTools with a per-server error surfaced instead of a generic 400.

title: DeepSeek API encoding error: Cannot convert argument to a ByteString because the character at index 299 has a value of 8212 which is greater than 255.

title: No changes in workspace for commit message when there a changes in workspace
author: unicornboat
evidence: The exact error string is thrown on main by `getGitDiff` in `apps/vscode/src/utils/git.ts`, which only runs `git --no-pager diff --staged --diff-filter=d` and `git --no-pager diff HEAD --diff-filter=d`. Neither command reports untracked files, and `--diff-filter=d` drops deletions, so a workspace whose SCM change count is made up of new/deleted files yields an empty diff. `generateCommitMsg` in `apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/commit-message-generator.ts` then surfaces it verbatim as `[Commit Generation Failed] No changes in workspace for commit message`.
notes: Fix is to include untracked files (e.g. `git add -N` / `--diff-filter` widening) before deciding there are no changes.

title: [BUG] Hub WebSocket rejects connections when authToken is empty string (regression in v0.0.43)
author: galaticpower
evidence: The reporter's root cause (read out of minified `dist/hub/daemon/entry.js`) does not match main: the client never depends on `CLINE_HUB_AUTH_TOKEN` — it reads the token from the discovery record (`record.authToken` in `sdk/packages/core/src/hub/client/index.ts:899` and `:1000`, plus `resolveLocalHubAuthToken`) and sends it as the `cline-hub-auth.<token>` subprotocol at `:352`, matching `readWebSocketAuthToken` in `sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/hub-websocket-server.ts:242`. The token-propagation bug behind the 1006 symptom was fixed two days after this was filed by commit 6138bdfe4 ("feat: Enforce a production singleton Cline Hub", #11372, 2026-06-10), whose description includes "Preserve and propagate auth tokens when retiring incompatible hubs" and "made discovery auth tokens required again".
notes: Fixed by 6138bdfe4 (#11372). The requested behavior (accept empty-token connections) should NOT be implemented — auth is required by design; the token is distributed via the discovery file.

title: [BUG] Hub WebSocket code 1006 — server generates random token rejecting no-auth clients

title: Even after enabling prompts, no system messages will pop up when completing tasks in plan mode
author: NGC13009
evidence: `enableNotifications` is a dead setting on main: it is declared in `apps/vscode/src/shared/AutoApprovalSettings.ts:25` and read/written by the settings plumbing (`updateAutoApprovalSettings.ts`, `updateTaskSettings.ts`, `newTask.ts`) and the webview toggle (`webview-ui/src/hooks/useAutoApproveActions.ts`), but nothing consumes it to emit a notification. title: [Windows specific] Cline: Cline is getting stuck for fraction of seconds whenever user tries to delete recent history
author: RajatNagoria
evidence: The deletion path on main is serial and re-lists everything per item: `apps/vscode/src/core/controller/task/deleteTasksWithIds.ts:35` loops `await deleteTaskWithId(controller, id)`, and each iteration does `await controller.deleteTaskFromState(id)` followed by a full `await controller.postStateToWebview()`. `deleteTaskFromState` in `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-history.ts:557` deletes the session and then re-runs `listHistory()`, which hydrates every remaining record and calls `getCachedTaskSize` (per-item disk stat). That is a plausible source of the observed sub-second UI stall, and it is worse on Windows where per-file stat is more expensive.
notes: QA-filed; maxpaulus43 could not reproduce on nightly but the reporter re-confirmed on both VS Code and JetBrains on Windows. History size is the likely missing variable. Fix direction: delete all ids first, then post state once, and avoid re-hydrating sizes on every delete.

title: DS4 says "The `execute_command` tool launches non-interactive `/bin/zsh` that doesn't source `.zshrc` ..."
author: DXXS
evidence: `getShellArgs` in `sdk/packages/shared/src/parse/shell.ts:52` returns `["-c", command]` for every posix shell — no `-l` and no `-i` — and `spawnAndCollect` in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts:136` spawns with `env: { ...process.env, ...config.env }`. zsh only sources `.zshrc` for interactive shells, so pyenv shims installed by `.zshrc` are never on PATH. This is now the default path in the extension too: `vscodeTerminalExecutionMode` defaults to `backgroundExec` (`apps/vscode/src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts:78`), which routes `execute_command` through this executor rather than a VS Code terminal.
notes: Needs a product decision, not just a patch: sourcing rc files makes agent commands match the user's interactive terminal (pyenv/nvm/asdf shims) but costs startup time and adds nondeterminism. Owner is @cline/shared (`getShellArgs`) plus the `shell` option in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/types.ts:304`.

title: Cline ignores documented .clinerules CLI-safety rules on Windows PowerShell, causing terminal stalls that need a window reload
author: asl202
evidence: The blamed root cause — dependence on VS Code shell-integration completion markers — is no longer the default path on main. `vscodeTerminalExecutionMode` defaults to `backgroundExec` (`apps/vscode/src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts:78`, set by commit 12703bf40 / #11972), which uses `spawnAndCollect` in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts` with piped stdio and a 30s default timeout that kills the whole process tree (`definitions.ts:460`, `bashTimeoutMs ?? 30000`). Indefinite hangs are therefore not possible in the default mode; only `vscodeTerminal` mode still uses the 1-hour `VSCODE_FOREGROUND_RUN_COMMANDS_TIMEOUT_MS` (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.ts:47`). No pre-flight command validator/rewriter exists on main.
notes: Two things bundled: (a) the PowerShell stall, addressed by the backgroundExec default + timeout in 12703bf40 (#11972); (b) a request for a validator that rewrites known-unsafe command forms against the user's own .clinerules, which is speculative and derived from one project's private ruleset. Closeable with an explanation of (a) and a pointer to hooks for (b).

title: Zed restart triggers ACP error -32601 "Method not found": session/load when reloading Cline
author: TAYUN
evidence: `AcpAgent.initialize` advertises `agentCapabilities: { loadSession: true }` at `apps/cli/src/acp/acpAgent.ts:94`, but the class implements only `initialize`, `newSession`, `prompt`, `cancel`, `setSessionMode`, `unstable_setSessionModel`, `setSessionConfigOption`, `authenticate` and `shutdown` — there is no `loadSession` method. `loadSession` is optional on the protocol's `Agent` interface (`@agentclientprotocol/sdk@0.16.1` `dist/acp.d.ts:699`, `loadSession?(params)`), so the unimplemented method falls through to -32601 exactly as the Zed logs show.
notes: Two valid fixes: implement `loadSession` (rehydrating from the CLI session store, which already supports resume) or stop advertising `loadSession: true` in the capability block. Not Windows-specific despite the report — the capability mismatch is unconditional.

title: @cline/agents usage fails during browser build
author: michaelhabibi
evidence: Still broken on main. `sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts:1` imports `createGateway` from `@cline/llms` and calls it at `:114`, and `sdk/packages/agents/bun.mts` externalizes `@cline/llms` (`const external = ["@cline/llms", "nanoid"]`). But `createGateway` is exported only from the node entry — `sdk/packages/llms/src/index.ts:94` (`export { createGateway, DefaultGateway } from "./providers/gateway"`) — and `sdk/packages/llms/src/index.browser.ts` has zero gateway exports. Since `@cline/llms` resolves to `./dist/index.browser.js` under the `browser` condition (`sdk/packages/llms/package.json` exports map), a Vite browser build gets `createGateway === undefined`, exactly as reported.
notes: Reported against 0.0.42; agents/llms are now 0.0.65 and the export gap is unchanged. `@cline/agents` self-describes as a 'Browser-safe agent runtime' with a `browser` export condition, so this is a real contract violation. Fix is either to re-export a browser-safe `createGateway` from `index.browser.ts` or to load it lazily behind the prebuilt-model path in `resolveRuntimeConfig`.

title: Cline: No endpoints found that support tool use. Try disabling "skills". error is shown trying to search using open router
author: RajatNagoria
evidence: The message is passed through verbatim from OpenRouter — grep for "No endpoints found" and "support tool use" returns nothing in /workspace. The actionable gap is on our side: `supportsTools` is declared in `apps/vscode/src/shared/api.ts:105` and never read anywhere in the repo, and `apps/vscode/src/core/controller/models/refreshOpenRouterModels.ts` only inspects `supported_parameters` for reasoning (`include_reasoning`/`reasoning`), never for `tools`. So Cline offers tool-incapable OpenRouter models (`openrouter/bodybuilder` in the report) and lets the provider 404 reach the user.
notes: QA-filed against both VS Code and JetBrains. Provider-side cause, Cline-side gap: wire `supportsTools` (populate it in refreshOpenRouterModels from `supported_parameters`) and gate the model list or the error message on it.

title: replace_in_file says SEARCH block does not match when displayed text exists as a partial-line match
author: martindye
evidence: The tool being described does not exist on main. There is no `replace_in_file` in the SDK tool definitions — `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.ts:664` registers `editor`, whose `replaceInFile` (`sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/editor.ts:170`) does plain substring matching via `countOccurrences` + `content.replace`, with no SEARCH/REPLACE blocks and no newline-terminated line spans. A partial-line match therefore succeeds on main, and the error text differs (`No replacement performed: text not found in <path>.` at `editor.ts:184`); the reported string "does not match anything in the file" appears nowhere in the repo. The `replace_in_file` names left in `apps/vscode/src/sdk/message-translator.ts` and `sdk-tool-policies.ts` are legacy-name mappings for rendering historical messages.
notes: Filed against 3.89.0. The exact-span line-boundary semantics that produced the misleading message were replaced by substring `old_str`/`new_str` editing at the SDK cutover.

title: Plan/Act separate OpenAI Compatible base URLs are coupled in v3.89.0
author: ikairz
evidence: Structurally still coupled on main. `openAiBaseUrl` is a single non-mode-scoped state key (`apps/vscode/src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts:120`), while the OpenAI-compatible model selection IS mode-scoped (`planModeOpenAiModelId` :163 / `actModeOpenAiModelId` :209). `resolveBaseUrl` in `apps/vscode/src/sdk/cline-session-factory.ts:607` maps `openai -> "openAiBaseUrl"` with no mode argument, so plan and act necessarily resolve the same URL. The same holds for every other provider in that map (anthropic, ollama, gemini, litellm, ...).
notes: Not a save/overwrite race — there is simply no per-mode base URL key. Fixing it means adding `planModeOpenAiBaseUrl`/`actModeOpenAiBaseUrl` (and deciding whether to do the same for the other providers in `resolveBaseUrl`) plus a migration.

title: Cline stops working after certain comands
author: AniGerm
evidence: The hang described (Cline waits forever for a terminal-completion signal, shows 'skipped', chat freezes until the extension is restarted) depended on VS Code shell integration, which is no longer the default. Commit 12703bf40 ("Improve VS Code terminal reliability: OSC 633 parser, exit codes, timeout handling", #11972, 2026-07-14) flipped `vscodeTerminalExecutionMode` to default `backgroundExec` (`apps/vscode/src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts:78`) and rewrote `VscodeTerminalProcess`/added `osc633Parser.ts`. In backgroundExec, commands run through `spawnAndCollect` (`sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts`) with piped stdio and a 30s default timeout that kills the process tree (`definitions.ts:460`).
notes: Filed against 3.89.0. Closeable with a request to retest; if it recurs, it would be a distinct backgroundExec bug (long-running servers hitting the 30s timeout is a different, expected behavior).

title: Cline CLI error during run_commands: emitt invalid json arguments
author: mmarras
evidence: The exact error text is still produced on main by `parseToolInput`/`parseToolArguments` in `sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts` (lines 1726 and 1771), and `parseToolArguments` is a plain `JSON.parse` with no repair. Two partial mitigations landed after the report: `292133989` (#11478) caps repeated DSML tool-call markup in `sdk/packages/core/src/session/services/message-builder.ts`, and `96b29d787` (#11803) adds `normalizeJsonLikeStringsForSchema` (`sdk/packages/shared/src/parse/json.ts`) used at `agent-runtime.ts:1366`. Neither covers the reported case: `repairMalformedToolCall` in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts:445` delegates to `parseJsonStream`, which returns the input unchanged when the text does not start with `{`/`[` — which is exactly the `<|DSML|tool_calls>` fragment the model emits here.

title: Cline: Improve code action starts execution in existing thread Instead of creating a new thread
author: kirtirajsinh-dot
evidence: On main all three code actions start a fresh task: `apps/vscode/src/core/controller/commands/improveWithCline.ts:40`, `explainWithCline.ts:33` and `fixWithCline.ts:13` all call `controller.initTask(...)`, and only the notebook branch (`notebookContext && controller.task`) reuses the active task. `SdkTaskStartCoordinator.initTask` (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-start-coordinator.ts:64`) calls `clearTask()` and then `sessions.startNewSession(...)` with a newly minted session id, so the described 'continues in the previous thread' behavior has no code path.

title: GCP Vertex AI provider exposes gemini-3.5-flash but Vertex returns 404 model not found
author: Hakai-Shin

title: Cline cli 3 does not show cost
author: mmarras
evidence: The CLI status bar renders cost purely from accumulated `totalCost` (`formatStatusBarUsageText` in `apps/cli/src/tui/components/status-bar.tsx`, gated by `shouldShowProviderUsageCost` in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/billing.ts`, which defaults to 'show'). `totalCost` is summed in `sdk/packages/core/src/services/usage.ts` from per-message `metrics.cost`, which `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts` derives from an upstream `cost` field or the catalog `n` pricing block. A proxied Azure Foundry model or a LiteLLM deployment has neither, so it accumulates 0 — and unlike the VS Code webview (`apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/settings/providers/OpenAICompatible.tsx`, which exposes `inputPrice`/`outputPrice`), nothing in `apps/cli/src` lets the user supply pricing.
notes: Two possible fixes: let the CLI accept per-model `inputPrice`/`outputPrice` like the VS Code OpenAI-compatible settings do, and/or read the `usage.cost` field LiteLLM already returns. Second reporter (zfleeman) confirms on 3.0.38 with LiteLLM.

title: Cline enters a high-volume request loop under repeated tool-use completions

title: [BUG] CLI run.start race condition with session.create causes total context loss — forensic evidence with log timestamps
author: galaticpower
evidence: Two of the three claims do not survive a read of main. Bug 1: `HubRuntimeHost.startSession` in `sdk/packages/core/src/hub/runtime-host/hub-runtime-host.ts` `await`s the `session.create` reply before returning, and `runTurn` (which sends `run.start`) is a separate later call, so the CLI cannot legitimately fire `run.start` first. Bug 2: `createSessionId` in `sdk/packages/shared/src/session/index.ts` is `${Date.now()}_${nanoid(5)}` over a 36-char alphabet, not a bare ULID, so same-millisecond collisions need a 1-in-60M nanoid clash — reuse of one id across hours is session resume, not collision. Bug 3 is plausible: `session.detach` still goes through the generic 30s request/reply path (`HUB_DEFAULT_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS` in `sdk/packages/shared/src/hub.ts`, pending-reply timeout in `sdk/packages/core/src/hub/client/index.ts`).
notes: High-effort report about context loss, so worth a maintainer read, but the stated timestamps are internally inconsistent (a CLI timeout logged 41s before the hub reply it supposedly missed) and two of three root causes are misdiagnosed. Ask for hub-daemon.log + cline.log from a current CLI (v4) before investing; the timeout message text has since changed to include requestId/clientId, which will make correlation easier.

author: agileramblings
evidence: Root cause found and reproduced on main. `apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/schemas.ts` builds a Zod union whose SSE branch precedes the streamableHttp branch and whose `transportType` legacy alias only maps the literal `"http"` (line 142); the SSE branch's fallback is `|| "sse"` (line 119). By contrast `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/mcp/config-loader.ts` (`mapLegacyTransportType`) does accept `transportType: "streamableHttp"`, so core and the VS Code host disagree.
notes: Two-line fix in `apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/schemas.ts`: make the SSE branch reject `transportType === "streamableHttp"` and let the streamableHttp branch accept it (mirroring `mapLegacyTransportType` in core). The reporter's secondary ask is also still valid — `Logger.error(\`Transport error for "${name}":\`, error)` in `McpHub.ts` and `StreamableHttpReconnectHandler.ts` logs an empty message. notes: If #11919's 're-does work after prodding' complaint is reproduced, check this resume-replay behaviour in the same session — they may share a cause.

title: CI/CD test coverage gap — message ID concatenation on repeated persistence (codec not idempotent for tool result messages)
author: Pauliehedron
evidence: Fixed on main: `sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/config/agent-message-codec.ts` now computes `const toolIdSuffix = \`_tool_${block.tool_use_id}\`` and emits `id: isPureToolResult || baseId.endsWith(toolIdSuffix) ? baseId : \`${baseId}${toolIdSuffix}\``, so re-encoding an already-encoded message cannot grow the id. The exact regression test the reporter asked for exists in `agent-message-codec.test.ts` ("A second round-trip of the split parts must not grow the ids"). `git log -S 'baseId.endsWith(toolIdSuffix)'` attributes it to 26037b17a "feat(core): default to agentic compaction (#12317)" (2026-07-21).
notes: Only the round-trip idempotence test was requested for the codec; the other coverage suggestions (persisted-artifact id assertions in local-runtime-host and the live messages contract test) are still not implemented, but the underlying defect is gone.

title: Plugin sandbox fails to initialize in VS Code extension 4.0.0 — plugin-sandbox-bootstrap.js not bundled
author: zk-0808
evidence: The packaging gap is still there on main. `sdk/packages/core/bun.mts` emits `plugin-sandbox-bootstrap.ts` as a separate entrypoint into `dist/extensions/`, and both CLI build scripts copy it (`apps/cli/bun.mts` copyFileSync into `./dist/extensions/plugin-sandbox-bootstrap.js`, `apps/cli/script/build.ts` likewise) — but `apps/vscode/esbuild.mjs` has no equivalent step, so none of the five candidates in `resolveBootstrap()` (`sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/plugin/plugin-sandbox.ts`) can resolve inside the extension's `dist/`, and the jiti fallback is unavailable because esbuild inlines it.
notes: Also a roadmap question the reporter asked and nobody answered: is the plugin subsystem supported in the VS Code extension at all? The extension does install plugins (`apps/vscode/src/core/controller/marketplace/marketplace-helpers.ts` writes to `~/.cline/plugins/_installed`) while never emitting the sandbox bootstrap, so plugins can appear 'Installed' with setup() silently never running. Related: #11065.

title: cline keeps crashing without any error inside a container
author: k-soomro
evidence: The crash is a Bun runtime segfault (`panic(main thread): Segmentation fault`, Bun v1.3.13, Linux arm64) inside the shipped standalone binary (`/usr/lib/node_modules/cline/bin/.cline`, produced by `apps/cli/script/build.ts` + `apps/cli/script/postinstall.mjs`). Main still pins the same runtime — `"bun": "1.3.13"` and `"packageManager": "bun@1.3.13"` in the root `package.json` — so nothing has changed that would clear it, and a second reporter hit it under WSL.
notes: Two independent reporters (lima/nerdctl on macOS arm64, and WSL on Windows) and a maintainer already said they were investigating, with no follow-up. Container/devcontainer usage is completely blocked, and the likely remedy is an upstream Bun bump in the pinned toolchain.

title: Cline buttons freeze after first save/accept; second suggested change cannot be saved
author: alex-farr1214
evidence: On main the manual-approval path opens the edit diff preview via `onToolApprovalAsk` -> `SdkDiffEditCoordinator.openForApproval` (apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts:317), and commit bcf8c1d03 (#12558, 2026-07-26) bounded that call because "a hung vscode.diff call ... on manual approval it delayed the approval ask indefinitely" — the exact freeze-after-first-edit/needs-extension-host-restart symptom reported. The 5s race guard is now at apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-diff-edit-coordinator.ts:30 and :285.
notes: Fix landed only on 2026-07-26 and has not shipped to the reporter's 4.0.2 build; worth asking the reporter (and daemenseth) to re-verify on a build containing bcf8c1d03 before closing.

title: Segmentation fault
author: CemreKArtworkss
evidence: Report body is a single screenshot with no stack trace, no command, and no repro steps; the "Cline Version 1.3.13.0" field is a Bun version, not a CLI version, so I could not map it to any code in apps/cli or sdk/packages/*. Nothing in the report names a symbol, file, or error string to check on main.

title: Cline VS Code extension v4.0.4 may slowly add orphaned terminal sessions which clogs Win OS
author: thomas-price
evidence: Terminals are deliberately never disposed on task abort (apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/terminal/VscodeTerminalManager.ts:456 keeps `//info.terminal.dispose()` commented out), so accumulation is possible in principle; however main now evicts and reclaims dead terminals via `evictTerminal` + `TerminalRegistry.queueTerminalForCleanup` / `disposeTerminalsPendingCleanup` (VscodeTerminalManager.ts:234-244, :312, VscodeTerminalRegistry.ts:92-104), all added in 12703bf40 (#11972, 2026-07-15) after this v4.0.4 report.
notes: Report is explicitly anecdotal ("more of a cautionary tale") with no repro. Ask the reporter to re-check terminal-process counts on a build containing #11972 before spending time on it.

title: CLI 3.0.34 crashes with `n.content.map is not a function` after long conversations / large MCP tool_result
author: zk-0808
evidence: Both decode paths on main still call `.map` on `message.content` with no `Array.isArray` guard: `agentMessageToMessageWithMetadata` (sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/config/agent-message-codec.ts:102) and `agentMessagesToMessages` (same file, :127). The encode direction does normalize (`normalizeContentBlocks`, :148), confirming the asymmetry the reporter describes. Last change to that file is 26037b17a (compaction default), so nothing has fixed it.
notes: PR #12032 (open, unmerged) adds the guard plus regression tests in agent-message-codec.test.ts. A guard is a band-aid — a maintainer should also decide whether something upstream is legitimately producing string `content` on an `AgentMessage`, since the type says `AgentMessagePart[]`.

title: Cline: While enabling MCP server, getting error like "MCP server fails with "MCP error -32000: Connection closed"
author: kirtirajsinh-dot
evidence: The exact failing path exists on main: `McpHub.toggleServerDisabledRPC` (apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts:1294) does deleteConnection -> connectToServer on every toggle and surfaces the raw transport error as `Failed to update server state: ...` (:1338). That file has had no commits since 2026-07-01, so the re-connect-on-toggle behavior is unchanged.
notes: Two independent reporters plus QA; one says it appears on IntelliJ 2026.1.4 but not 2025.3, which points at the shared McpHub/standalone core rather than JetBrains UI. Suspect a teardown race in deleteConnection before connectToServer.

title: Cerebras `zai-glm-4.7` reasoning-only responses are misreported as "Connection error"
author: seyfigo
evidence: The literal string "Connection error." appears nowhere in apps/ or sdk/ on main; it is the `openai` npm SDK's APIConnectionError message, and `openai` is no longer used in any request path on main (its only reference is a doc comment in apps/vscode/src/shared/net.ts:25). On main a reasoning-only, budget-exhausted turn hits `finishReason === "max-tokens"` with no tool calls and throws MAX_TOKENS_INCOMPLETE_TURN_MESSAGE — "Model reached the maximum output token limit before completing the turn" (sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts:45-46, :673-675), which is the user-friendly message the reporter asked for.

title: Destructive shell commands run without approval when the model sets requires_approval=false
author: Jiangrong-W
evidence: The blamed file `apps/vscode/src/core/task/tools/handlers/ExecuteCommandToolHandler.ts` does not exist on main (apps/vscode/src/core/task only contains focus-chain/ and tools/subagent/), and `requires_approval` appears nowhere in sdk/packages/* — the SDK `run_commands` tool has no such field. Approval on main is decided host-side from user settings only: `SdkInteractionCoordinator` consults `request.policy.autoApprove` / `shouldAutoApproveTool` (apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-interaction-coordinator.ts:90) which resolves through `isToolAutoApproved` (apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-tool-policies.ts:49-73).

Adjacent nuance worth noting on main: `isToolAutoApproved` maps every command tool to a single `actions.executeSafeCommands` toggle with no destructive-pattern check, so that toggle auto-approves all commands (it defaults to false in DEFAULT_AUTO_APPROVAL_SETTINGS).

title: [ErrorService] Logging exception after the Gemini API stopped accepting requests from unrestricted API keys on June 19, 2026
author: AliOko
evidence: The reporter's log lines come from the retired 3.x stack: neither "[Prompt variant] Selected" nor the `TODO_SECTION` prompt component exists anywhere in apps/ or sdk/ on main (apps/vscode/src/core/prompts now only contains responses.ts). `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` is still a valid catalog entry (sdk/packages/llms/src/catalog/catalog.generated.ts:2484), but the reported 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT carries no field-level detail, so I could not tie it to any request builder on main.

title: [SDK] Session metadata is not passed to tool calls
author: eugenelee0420
evidence: Confirmed on main: `StartSessionInput.sessionMetadata` exists (sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/host/runtime-host.ts:115) and is only used for the session record (local-runtime-host.ts:529, :772), while the `agentConfig` object built in local-runtime-host.ts:625-694 never sets `toolContextMetadata`. Consequently `session-runtime-orchestrator.ts:847-851` builds the tool context from only `modelSupportsImages` + `this.config.toolContextMetadata` + the internal telemetry key, so custom tools see no session metadata.
notes: Needs a small API decision: forward `input.sessionMetadata` into `toolContextMetadata`, or expose `toolContextMetadata` on StartSessionInput (it is currently unreachable from ClineCore.start). Owner: @cline/core.

title: PROVIDER_API_KEY_MAP has a dead `claude_code` entry (provider id is `claude-code`)
author: mc856
evidence: Verified verbatim on main: `claude_code: "apiKey"` at apps/vscode/src/sdk/cline-session-factory.ts:337 inside PROVIDER_API_KEY_MAP (declared :300), while the canonical id in the ApiProvider union is `"claude-code"` (apps/vscode/src/shared/api.ts:6) and `resolveApiKey` looks the map up by that id (cline-session-factory.ts:424). The lookup therefore always returns undefined.

Two contributors are waiting on direction.

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate Developer Beta (Apple Silicon): CLI binary is killed by AMFI (CODE SIGNING: cs_invalid_page)
author: classload-ux
evidence: The release pipeline has no macOS signing at all: .github/workflows/cli-publish.yml builds all six platform binaries in one cross-compile step (`bun script/build.ts --install-native-variants`, line ~148) and then publishes straight to npm, and neither the workflow nor apps/cli/script/build.ts contains any `codesign`/`notarytool` step (build.ts only lists `{ os: "darwin", arch: "arm64" }` targets at :62-63). That matches the reporter's `Signature=adhoc / TeamIdentifier=not set`.

Currently only reproducible on the macOS 27 developer beta, but it becomes a hard install-blocker for every macOS user when 27 ships. Reporter's workaround is re-running `codesign --force --deep --sign -` locally.

title: Zed - ACP model selector in only shows 2 hardcoded options, ignores authenticated providers
author: vosonha89
evidence: Confirmed on main: `ACP_AUTH_METHODS` holds only `cline` and `openai-codex` (apps/cli/src/acp/auth.ts:9-12); `buildProviderConfigOption` maps over exactly that constant (apps/cli/src/acp/acpAgent.ts:563-574); `setSessionConfigOption` rejects anything else with `Unknown provider` via `isAcpAuthMethodId` (acpAgent.ts:316-321); and `newSession` defaults to `cline` / `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` (acpAgent.ts:130-133) without consulting ProviderSettingsManager or the client's default_config_options.

Real financial impact: users silently get billed on the Cline hosted tier while believing they configured a self-paid provider. A contributor (@edobusy) has offered to implement the merge of ProviderSettingsManager providers into the selector and is waiting for direction.

title: MCP server initialization timeout (1500ms) should be configurable
author: dormiduende
evidence: Both constants the reporter reverse-engineered from the bundle are literal in source on main: `MCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000` and `MCP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 1_500` (sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/mcp/client.ts:41-42), and the latter is passed directly as the `initialize` request timeout (:165-175). No server config field feeds it — the only `timeoutMs` in this area is `CreateMcpToolsOptions.timeoutMs` for tool calls (extensions/mcp/types.ts:32, tools.ts:32).
notes: Well-specified and agent-fixable: thread a per-server (and/or global) initialize timeout from cline_mcp_settings.json through McpServerRegistration into client.ts:175. Note the connect path already retries twice (newline then framed protocol mode), so the effective startup wait is ~3s.

title: Operations button in Stock tab returns "unexpected server error"
author: operationsaratex-hub
evidence: The report describes a bug in the reporter's own "Custom Stock Manager" web application (log in, click the Stock tab, click Operations), not in Cline: no Cline surface, command, setting, provider or error string is referenced, and nothing in apps/ or sdk/ contains an "Operations"/"Stock" UI.

title: Commands don't get executed
author: matthias-bay
evidence: This is exactly the failure mode fixed by 12703bf40 (#11972, 2026-07-15), which added apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-terminal-execution-mode.ts. Its header comment states that `vscodeTerminal` mode "is meaningless — and silently a no-op — on the standalone (JetBrains/CLI) build, where vscode.window.createTerminal is a stub", and that a `vscodeTerminal` value saved by the real VS Code extension leaks into standalone sessions through the shared ~/.cline state; `getEffectiveTerminalExecutionMode` (:32-37) now clamps standalone hosts to `backgroundExec`, and it is applied at apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-session-host.ts:146.
notes: Silent no-op with a fabricated 'exit code 0, no output' result is the worst class of bug (the model acts on fake success), and three reporters hit it. Fix is on main but the JetBrains plugin pins its own cline-core build, so a maintainer should confirm which plugin release first carries #11972 before closing.

title: Cline: User gets insufficient balance error
author: RajatNagoria
evidence: The error is server-originated: main only classifies it, via `code === "insufficient_credits"` in SdkController (apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts:1098-1111) and ClineError.getErrorType -> ClineErrorType.Balance (apps/vscode/src/services/error/ClineError.ts:163-165). I found no account-switching code on main that recomputes or caches a balance, so I cannot locate a client-side defect for the reported org->personal switch.
notes: Filed by QA with a video; the reporter notes the account display flips to 'Cline external' after the failure, which suggests the active-account/credential selection is not propagating to the request rather than a genuine zero balance. Likely needs backend/account-service investigation, which is outside this repo.

title: Generate Git Commit Message does not work for add only
author: gregtakacs
evidence: Confirmed on main: `getGitDiff` only runs `git --no-pager diff --staged --diff-filter=d` and then falls back to `git --no-pager diff HEAD --diff-filter=d` (apps/vscode/src/utils/git.ts:204-215). Neither command reports untracked files, so a workspace whose only change is a brand-new unstaged file yields an empty diff and throws `No changes in workspace for commit message` (:216-218), which commit-message-generator.ts:93 renders as `[Commit Generation Failed] ...`. No commits have touched either file since 2026-07-01.
notes: Agent-fixable: include untracked files in the unstaged fallback (e.g. `git add --intent-to-add`-style listing via `git status --porcelain` plus `git diff --no-index /dev/null <file>`), matching what the VS Code SCM view shows the user.

title: team_run_task sync mode reports status "running" after the task has completed
author: Statusnone420
evidence: Confirmed verbatim on main: the sync branch of the `team_run_task` tool resolves with `mode: "sync", status: "running"` alongside the message "Task dispatched to ... and completed in sync mode" (sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/team-tools.ts:541-550), while the async branch correctly returns `status: "queued"` (:513-521).

One-line source fix plus a TeamRunTaskToolResultSchema update; a contributor (@CoderSufiyan) says they have the patch and regression test ready and is waiting for a maintainer.

title: team_run_task gives misleading "Teammate was not found" error when passed the lead agentId
author: Statusnone420
evidence: Confirmed on main: `routeToTeammate` rejects with the generic `Teammate "<id>" was not found` when the member exists but its role is not "teammate" (sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/team/multi-agent.ts:1018-1022); `shutdownTeammate` has the identical conflation at :908-911. team_run_task forwards the id straight into that path (team-tools.ts:533-540).

title: math fomula can't be rendered
author: d34advtscvz4
evidence: Not JetBrains-specific: the shared webview markdown renderer on main registers only remark-gfm and three local plugins, with rehype-highlight as the sole rehype plugin (apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/common/MarkdownBlock.tsx:79-85). There is no remark-math / rehype-katex anywhere in apps/vscode/webview-ui, so `$$...$$` and LaTeX environments render as raw text in VS Code too.

title: Abnormal Huge Context Detected
author: Fireqtian
evidence: A cumulative-metrics inflation bug of exactly this shape (per-message token estimates derived from cumulative request metrics, producing wildly oversized context and spurious auto-compaction) was fixed in be97d951f (#12022, 2026-07-01) — see the regression test "does not treat cumulative request metrics as per-message token counts" (sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context/compaction.test.ts:49) guarding `createTokenEstimator` in sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context/compaction-shared.ts. Whether the reporter's 4.0.6 build predates that commit is not determinable from the issue.
notes: Spurious auto-compaction destroys conversation context, so this is worth confirming rather than closing. Ask for the provider/model (field was left blank) and the task's reported input/cache token metrics; a wrong estimator or a model whose maxTokens ~ contextWindow both funnel through resolveMaxInputTokens in compaction.ts:99-113.

title: Follow-up questions are not rendered correctly
author: thunderstorm010
evidence: On main the follow-up options reach the webview as a plain `string[]`: the ask_question tool validates its input against `AskQuestionInputSchema`, which requires `options: z.array(z.string().min(1)).min(2).max(5)` (sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/schemas.ts:258-271), and the host just JSON-stringifies them into the `followup` ask (apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-interaction-coordinator.ts:123-134) for OptionsButtons.tsx:38 to render. A single concatenated string should therefore be rejected by zod before rendering, so I could not confirm the concatenation path the reporter (and PR #12085) assume.
notes: Reported with a local llama-server gemma model. A maintainer should get the raw tool-call payload before merging PR #12085, which normalizes the concatenated shape in the webview — if the schema is really rejecting it upstream, the UI fix papers over a small-model tool-call parsing problem in the wrong layer.

title: Cline bot regularly stuck in thinking mode
author: LeoLGC
evidence: Same symptom, same environment class (VS Code Remote SSH, long-running command turns) and same code area as #12079 — the VS Code terminal integration under apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/terminal/ (osc633Parser.ts, VscodeTerminalProcess.ts). A Cline maintainer (saoudrizwan) replied to this issue with nothing but a link to a comment on #12079.

title: When using OpenRouter's `Preset` models in Cline, it keeps repeating the same response.
author: hiro-gj
evidence: OpenRouter presets are simply unimplemented: grepping `preset` across sdk/packages/llms/src returns no matches, so `openrouter/auto@preset/presets-test` is passed through as an opaque model id with no catalog entry (hence the 400s on other spellings). The repetition is the expected shape of the no-tool-call path: when an assistant turn contains no tool calls the runtime appends a completion reminder and loops (sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts:681-695), which a preset member model without tool-call support will never escape.
notes: Two separable asks: (1) first-class OpenRouter preset support in @cline/llms including model metadata; (2) the loop is now bounded by the consecutive-mistake tracker's `completion_without_submit` reason (sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/safety/mistake-tracker.ts:169-176), tightened for VS Code in e4091c368.

title: Command execution shows "skipped" in Cline terminal and hangs on "thinking" — requires extension restart to recover
author: nadahmed
evidence: The owning code is on main under apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/terminal/ (osc633Parser.ts, VscodeTerminalProcess.ts, VscodeTerminalManager.ts). Commit 12703bf40 (#11972, 2026-07-15) rewrote OSC 633 parsing, moved to the newer shell-execution-end API and added unobserved-command eviction (VscodeTerminalManager.ts:234-244), but the SSH/no-shell-integration case still falls back to a timeout-and-scrape path, which the maintainer (dominiccooney) states in-thread "won't get stuck, but they were never great and still are not great".

Two distinct sub-cases are being conflated: markerless/SSH terminals (fallback scrape) and local terminals where a malformed command breaks the prompt. One reporter also found disabling Checkpoints stopped an infinite `schedule assistant presentation` log loop — worth checking independently.

title: Cline CLI Crashes on Launch (Windows, regardless of args)
author: kieronlanning
evidence: The crash is a Bun runtime panic (`panic(main thread): Segmentation fault`) inside the compiled `@cline/cli-windows-x64` binary, not a JS-level throw; `main` still pins the same runtime (`package.json` `packageManager: bun@1.3.13`, `.github/workflows/cli-publish.yml` uses `bun-version: 1.3.13`) and still ships single-file Bun executables from `apps/cli/script/build.ts` (win32 -> `windows` target). title: [Cerebras] "Connection error" on every request while identical curl to api.cerebras.ai succeeds (Cline 4.0.6, VS Code 1.127.0, macOS arm64)
author: aashu4uiit
evidence: The generic `Connection error.` string comes from the Stainless-generated `@cerebras/cerebras_cloud_sdk` client used by the retired handler at `apps/vscode/src/core/api/providers/cerebras.ts` (present on the `legacy-extension` branch, absent on `main` — `apps/vscode/src/core/api/` contains only `index.ts`). On `main` Cerebras is a plain `openai-compatible` builtin (`sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtins.ts` id `cerebras`, baseUrl `https://api.cerebras.ai/v1`) driven by the AI SDK, whose network failures surface as `Cannot connect to API: <cause>` (`@ai-sdk/provider-utils` `handleFetchError`) — i.e. the error transparency the reporter asks for already exists.
notes: Both the failing code path and the poor error message belong to the legacy 4.0.x marketplace build. Ask the reporter to retest on an SDK-based build; if it still fails the new message will name the real cause (DNS/TLS/proxy).

title: attempt_completion frames all post-completion messages as feedback - no branch for new/unrelated requests
author: sapiens-aquilae
evidence: The hardcoded string the report blames does not exist anywhere on `main`: `rg 'Consider their input to continue the task'` and `rg 'attempt completion again'` across the repo (excluding node_modules) both return nothing. The completion tool itself was renamed — `sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/orchestration/runtime-builder.ts` aliases `attempt_completion` to `submit_and_exit`, and `sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/host/local-runtime-host.ts` treats it purely as a telemetry/lifecycle signal; post-completion input arrives as an ordinary new turn via `prepareTurnInput`, with no feedback wrapper.
notes: The only `attempt_completion` text left in `apps/vscode/src/core/prompts/responses.ts` is the tool-use reminder, not a post-completion wrapper.

title: search_files mangles absolute Windows paths, suppresses the error, then blames the model
author: martindye
evidence: On `main` the search tool takes no path argument at all: `SearchCodebaseInputSchema` in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/schemas.ts` is `{ queries: string[] }`, and `createSearchTool` in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.ts` always passes the fixed `config.cwd` to the executor, so there is nothing to join onto the workspace root. Failures are also no longer swallowed — the executor wrapper returns `{ success: false, error: 'Search failed: ...' }` instead of `Found 0 results`. The model-capability nag is gone too: `sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/safety/mistake-tracker.ts` `buildMistakeLimitStopMessage` emits a generic message, and e4091c368 (#12561) removed the max-mistakes setting. `apps/vscode` only keeps `search_files` as a display alias (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/message-translator.ts`).
notes: Needs a human only to redirect @AriaZhao-coder, who announced a PR to fix path joining and error suppression in code that no longer exists on `main`. Worth noting separately that `main` currently cannot search outside the workspace at all — that would be a new feature request, not this bug.

title: Unbounded hub-daemon.log from zombie sessions degrades Dashboard performance
author: Cya030
evidence: Both halves are still present on `main`. `sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/handlers/run-handlers.ts` sets `HUB_RUN_HEARTBEAT_MS = 30_000` and `setInterval` unconditionally emits `logHubMessage("warn", "run.heartbeat", ...)` for as long as `runTurn` is outstanding, with no cap or stuck-run abort. `sdk/packages/core/src/hub/daemon/index.ts` `openDetachedHubLogFile()` does `openSync(logPath, "a")` on `~/.cline/data/logs/hub-daemon.log`, and a repo-wide grep for log rotation/size limits in `sdk/packages/core/src`, `apps/cline-hub/src` and `apps/cli/src` returns nothing.
notes: Two separable fixes: (1) size/retention-capped rotation for hub-daemon.log, (2) a run-level timeout so `run.start` sessions cannot heartbeat for days. The reporter's `elapsedMs` values (~598,586,345 ms ≈ 7 days) match a run that never settles.

title: Cline Nightly regularly exceeds context limit with ChatGPT 5.5 instead of compacting properly
author: Qnected
evidence: Compaction fires only when the estimated transcript crosses `COMPACTION_TRIGGER_RATIO` (0.9) of `resolveEffectiveMaxInputTokens` in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context/compaction-shared.ts`, and that budget comes from the catalog, which lists `gpt-5.5` at contextWindow 1,050,000 / maxInputTokens 922,000 for `openai-native` in `sdk/packages/llms/src/catalog/catalog.generated.ts` — far above the ~400K the reporter observes. Token counting is a crude `Math.ceil(chars / 3)` (`sdk/packages/shared/src/llms/tokens.ts`), and there is no context-window-exceeded recovery anywhere (grep for `context_length_exceeded` / `isContextWindowError` across `sdk` and `apps` returns nothing), so an overflow is fatal rather than triggering a forced compaction.
notes: Two candidate root causes to separate: (a) the catalog's gpt-5.5 input budget overstating the real limit, (b) no fallback that force-compacts and retries when the provider reports context overflow. 10cb9bd97 (#12142, 'Add compaction budget hardening', 2026-07-09) and 4a97b46f5 (#12217) landed after this report and may have partially addressed (a).

title: HDPO
author: Harsh97711
evidence: Body is `> HAV FFO` quoted from a commit-line comment on 7cdaca0; there is no surface, version, reproduction, or identifiable symbol to look up anywhere in /workspace. Same author as 12117 ('GDPO'), which is equally contentless.
notes: Auto-closeable.

title: Telemetry is still initialized and shutdown even when disabled, causing slow VS Code quit on macOS
author: zyonbao
evidence: `apps/vscode/src/services/telemetry/TelemetryProviderFactory.ts` `getDefaultConfigs()` never consults the user's `telemetrySetting` or VS Code's `telemetry.telemetryLevel`; it pushes a PostHog config whenever `isPostHogConfigValid(posthogConfig)` and an OpenTelemetry config whenever `getValidOpenTelemetryConfig()` returns one, then `createProvider` eagerly constructs `PostHogClientProvider.getClient()` / `new OpenTelemetryClientProvider(otelConfig)` and awaits `.initialize()`. Teardown always pays the cost too: `apps/vscode/src/common.ts` `tearDown()` calls `PostHogClientProvider.getInstance().dispose()` and `telemetryService.dispose()` unconditionally, and `apps/vscode/src/extension.ts` `deactivate()` awaits it.
notes: The 'disabled means no events sent, not no machinery' conclusion is exactly what the code does. The ~6s quit delay is the reporter's measurement and still needs confirming, but the early-return-a-no-op-provider fix they suggest is straightforward and also answers their privacy question.

title: GDPO
author: Harsh97711
evidence: Body is the issue template with `1. GDPO 2. HDPO 3. MILESONE 4. RTOP/`, version `01`, empty repro steps. Nothing maps to any file, setting, or symbol in /workspace. Same author and same day as 12112.
notes: Auto-closeable alongside 12112.

title: CLINE chat window buffer gets too large
author: billsargent
evidence: The chat list is already virtualized (`apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/chat-view/components/layout/MessagesArea.tsx` renders through `react-virtuoso`), so the growth is the retained message array and per-row content, not DOM nodes. There is no user-facing way to prune old turns without starting a new task — the only trimming on `main` is model-side compaction (`sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context/compaction.ts`). The PR the maintainer pointed at, #11967, merged 2026-07-08 as 'perf(sdk): stop listSessions hot loop from hanging the extension host', which addresses a different hot loop.
notes: Maintainer @dominiccooney already engaged. The ask (prune completed/irrelevant sections of a live conversation from the UI) is a product decision on top of the existing compaction machinery.

title: `StreamableHttpReconnectHandler` loops forever when server returns `200` + immediately-closed SSE on `GET /mcp` (fast-flap pattern)
author: boghyon
evidence: Both mechanisms the reporter traced are verbatim present on `main`. In `apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/StreamableHttpReconnectHandler.ts` the reconnect loop does `await this.callbacks.connectToServer(); ...; this.attempts = 0` immediately on success, so the `maxAttempts: 6` cap in `DEFAULT_RECONNECT_CONFIG` is never reached under fast-flap. And `apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts` constructs `new StreamableHttpReconnectHandler(name, {...})` inside the `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` branch of `connectToServer`, so every reconnect also creates a fresh handler with `attempts = 0`. The `404 -> 405` GET shim they cite is likewise still the only special case in `McpHub`'s fetch wrapper.
notes: @chaitanya202's analysis in the comments is correct and worth reading: the retry budget needs to be server-scoped (owned by McpHub) with a stability window before reset, not transport-scoped. A design call is needed so the Linear-MCP idle-disconnect case #9642 fixed does not regress.

title: Cannot not use (in ACP mode) without an account
author: liar666
evidence: `apps/cli/src/acp/auth.ts` hardcodes `ACP_AUTH_METHODS = [{ id: 'cline' }, { id: 'openai-codex' }]`, and `apps/cli/src/acp/acpAgent.ts` `newSession()` throws `RequestError.authRequired(...)` unless `this.authResult` is set or `process.env.CLINE_API_KEY` is present. `tryRestoreAuth()` only probes persisted credentials for those two provider ids, so a user who configured their own OpenAI-compatible provider via `cline auth` / config files is still forced through the Cline sign-in — exactly the reported behavior. `initialize()` also advertises only those two `authMethods` to the ACP client.
notes: Owned by `apps/cli`. Fix direction: let `newSession` accept any already-configured provider (respect `CLINE_PROVIDER`/persisted provider settings) instead of gating on the two OAuth methods; note the default model is also hardcoded to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` in the same function.

title: Unable to find/change Cline System Commands/Prompts
author: deehill
evidence: Both things the reporter says are missing exist on `main`: custom instructions are surfaced through `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/cline-rules/ClineRulesToggleModal.tsx` (rules/workflows toggles), and the Ollama request timeout they wanted is a real setting — `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/settings/providers/OllamaProvider.tsx` binds `requestTimeoutMs` (default 30000), declared in `apps/vscode/src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts`. Their own log shows `llama3.1:8b` emitting a bare `ask_followup_question` tool call and the stream aborting, which is small-local-model behavior, not a Cline defect.
notes: Support request. Worth a docs pointer: there is no supported way to replace the system prompt wholesale, only to add rules/instructions — that expectation gap is the real content of the issue.

title: CLI: "text part msg_... not found" streaming from OpenAI-compatible backend that omits `content` key on empty deltas (e.g. llama.cpp server-rocm)
author: andlumm
evidence: The `msg_`-prefixed part id is the tell: `@ai-sdk/openai`'s Responses transport emits `text-start` only on `response.output_item.added` with `item.type === 'message'` (id = `value.item.id`) and `text-delta` with `id: value.item_id`; `ai`'s `streamText` recorder then enqueues `error: 'text part ' + part.id + ' not found'` when a delta arrives with no matching start. Cline routes LiteLLM through that transport: `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtins.ts` declares the `litellm` builtin with `protocol: "openai-responses"`. The plain `openai-compatible` path would have used the fixed id `txt-0`, so the reporter's chat-completions-shaped analysis is slightly off but the failure is real and provider-config-driven.
notes: Two things to decide: whether `litellm` should default to `openai-responses` at all given LiteLLM commonly fronts chat-completions backends, and whether `@cline/llms` should tolerate a text delta with no start (synthesize the start) rather than letting the AI SDK error the run out. The reporter did careful A/B isolation; their bug is real even though the stated mechanism is chat-completions-flavored.

title: Git commit --amend should not be considered a "safe command"
author: BroadlyWhitaker
evidence: There is no safe-command classifier anywhere on `main`. `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-tool-policies.ts` `isToolAutoApproved` resolves every command tool (`isCommandTool` = `run_commands` | `execute_command`) to the single flag `settings.actions.executeSafeCommands`, and `apps/vscode/src/shared/AutoApprovalSettings.ts` still names that field `executeSafeCommands` while the webview labels it 'Execute commands' (`apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/auto-approve-menu/constants.ts`). So enabling it auto-approves `git commit --amend` and everything else.
notes: Maintainer @dominiccooney already flagged this as a migration regression and asked @reneehuang1/@saoudrizwan whether to rename the option or rebuild a real safe-command list, and whether to align with the CLI (which has no 'safe' concept). That is a product decision, not an agent-fixable bug. Related discussion on #12150.

title: CLI crashes after ~15s — session.create times out, hub-daemon reports kanban/dist/entry.js MODULE_NOT_FOUND
author: edwinhati
evidence: `sdk/packages/core/src/hub/daemon/index.ts` `resolveDaemonEntryPath()` derives the daemon entry from `import.meta.url` of whichever copy of `@cline/core` spawned it, so a hub launched from a different package (the globally installed `kanban`, which embeds core) records a `.../kanban/dist/...` entry path that breaks when that package is upgraded — matching the reported `Cannot find module ".../kanban/dist/entry.js"` plus `EADDRINUSE` on 127.0.0.1:25463. There is no `kanban` entry path in this repo (grep across `apps/cli/src`, `apps/cline-hub/src`, `sdk/packages/core/src` finds only the CLI's `kanban` launcher in `apps/cli/src/commands/kanban.ts`). The 30s client-side ceiling is real too: `sdk/packages/core/src/hub/client/index.ts` errors with `Hub command ... timed out`, and `hub-runtime-host.ts` `recoverLocalHubStartupDeadlock` only recovers when the hub is *idle*, not when it is degraded.
notes: Cross-product hub-ownership problem in the shared-daemon design, not a kanban packaging bug alone. Worth deciding whether the daemon entry path should be re-resolved (and the discovery record invalidated) when the recorded path no longer exists, and whether `recoverLocalHubStartupDeadlock` should also fire for a degraded-but-listening hub.

title: Rules, hooks and workflows should NOT be saved in ~/Documents
author: wolterkam
evidence: Still hardcoded on `main` in both layers. `sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts` defines `resolveDocumentsClineDirectoryPath()` as `join(HOME_DIR, "Documents", "Cline")` and feeds it into `resolveHooksConfigSearchPaths`, `resolveRulesConfigSearchPaths` (via `resolveDocumentsExtensionPath("Rules")`), `resolveWorkflowsConfigSearchPaths` and `resolvePluginConfigSearchPaths`, with no `$XDG_*` handling. `apps/vscode/src/core/storage/disk.ts` goes further and `mkdir`s them unprompted — `ensureRulesDirectoryExists`, `ensureWorkflowsDirectoryExists`, `ensureMcpServersDirectoryExists`, `ensureHooksDirectoryExists` — and `ensureMcpServersDirectoryExists()` is invoked when McpHub is constructed in `apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts`.
notes: Maintainer @dominiccooney already agreed and added that the path is watched and aggressively recreated. Needs a product decision on the target location (`~/.cline` vs XDG) and a migration for existing users; touches `@cline/shared` paths plus every app that calls the `ensure*DirectoryExists` helpers.

title: CLI does not save general settings
author: PlasmaHH
evidence: The `/settings` toggles only mutate the in-memory `Config`. `apps/cli/src/runtime/run-interactive.ts` wires `onAutoApproveChange` to `setInteractiveAutoApprove`, which in `apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/approvals.ts` just sets `autoApproveAllRef.current` and calls `applyInteractiveAutoApproveOverride({ targetPolicies: config.toolPolicies, ... })`; `onCompactionModeChange` calls `applyCliCompactionMode` in `apps/cli/src/utils/compaction-mode.ts`, which assigns `config.compaction = {...}` and returns. Neither writes to disk, and `apps/cli/src/tui/contexts/session-context.tsx` re-seeds state on startup from `config.toolPolicies["*"]?.autoApprove !== false` — so every restart falls back to the file/default value.
notes: Severity is driven by the safety direction the reporter calls out: because the in-memory auto-approve override is lost, a user who turned auto-approve off gets it back on at next launch. Fix belongs in `apps/cli` (persist through the same store `/settings` reads from).

title: Error: JSON error injected into SSE stream
author: kieronlanning
evidence: The literal string is not produced by Cline or its shipped deps — grep for `JSON error injected` across /workspace (including node_modules) returns nothing — so it is an upstream payload (OpenRouter injecting an error object into an in-flight SSE stream) surfaced verbatim. What is grounded on `main` is that Cline has no mid-stream recovery: `openrouter` is a plain `openai-compatible` builtin in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtins.ts`, and there is no request/stream retry configuration in `sdk/packages/llms/src` (grep for `maxRetries` there returns nothing), so a mid-stream error aborts the turn.
notes: As filed there are no repro steps, model, or logs. Still worth a human because the underlying gap — mid-stream provider errors kill a long session with no retry or resume — is real and matches other reports in this batch (12094-style interruptions). Ask for the model id and whether it correlates with a specific OpenRouter upstream.

title: Prompt caching setting persists across Plan/Act mode models
author: rcamarda390
evidence: The reporter's inspection of `globalState.json` matches the schema on `main`: `apps/vscode/src/shared/storage/state-keys.ts` declares `awsBedrockUsePromptCache` under 'Global configuration (not mode-specific)', while the Bedrock model selection is per-mode (`planModeAwsBedrockCustomModelBaseId`, `planModeAwsBedrockCustomSelected`, and the act-mode counterparts). There are no `planMode*/actMode*` prompt-cache keys. The SDK carries the same single-value shape — `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtins.ts` maps the setting to the path `aws.usePromptCache`, read once in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/compat.ts`.
notes: Needs a design choice between the reporter's two options: make prompt caching mode-scoped like the model selection, or ignore the flag for models whose ModelInfo lacks the `prompt-cache` capability (the catalog already tracks that capability, which makes option 2 cheap and fixes the plain non-split case too).

title: Cline: Mac Specific: Unable to install certain MCP servers from the Marketplace
author: kirtirajsinh-dot
evidence: The install path exists on `main` and is short: `apps/vscode/src/core/controller/marketplace/installMarketplaceEntry.ts` -> `installMarketplaceEntryFromCatalog` -> `installMcpMarketplaceEntry` (`marketplace-helpers.ts`) -> `installMcpServer` in `sdk/packages/core/src/services/mcp-install.ts`, then `controller.mcpHub.reconcileMcpServersFromSettingsRPC()`. I verified the settings file is not split-brained — `installMcpServer` falls back to `resolveDefaultMcpSettingsPath()` (`~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json`) and `SdkController.ts` constructs `McpHub` with `path.dirname(resolveDefaultMcpSettingsPath())`, so both sides read the same file. Errors are surfaced (`MarketplaceView.tsx` `handleInstall` sets `error` on throw), so a completely silent no-op is not explained by the code I read.
notes: QA-filed with a video, so the repro is cheap. Two leads worth checking first: (a) `isMcpInstalled` matches by the first install arg / entry id / entry name, so a name mismatch in those specific catalog entries would make a successful install look like a no-op; (b) those servers are `uvx`/`docker`-style stdio servers, and macOS GUI VS Code does not inherit the login-shell PATH — compare with 099c6179e, which fixed exactly that class of problem for the desktop app.

title: Cline: Installed MCP server gets removed from MCP server section when user relaunch IDE after turning off installed MCP server
author: RajatNagoria
evidence: `apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts` `getServers()` deliberately returns only enabled servers (`this.connections.filter((conn) => !conn.server.disabled)`), but `listLocalMarketplaceInstalledEntries` in `apps/vscode/src/core/controller/marketplace/marketplace-helpers.ts` builds the Customise > installed list from `controller.mcpHub?.getServers()` and then sets `enabled: server.disabled !== true` — a field that can never be false, proving the intent was to include disabled servers. So a disabled MCP server is filtered out of the installed list, which is exactly the reported disappearance. The disabled state itself persists correctly (`toggleServerDisabledRPC` writes `disabled: true` to the settings file and `connectToServer` pushes a disconnected stub connection for it), and the MCP configuration view is fine because it goes through `notifyWebviewOfServerChanges` -> `getSortedMcpServers`, which does not filter.
notes: Small, well-localized fix: give `listLocalMarketplaceInstalledEntries` (and probably `isMcpInstalled`, which has the same `getServers()` dependency and would report a disabled server as not installed) an all-connections accessor instead of the enabled-only `getServers()`.

title: Spawn agents to review changes sometimes is breaking lines per word in TUI
author: gbrennon
evidence: The subagent/team transcript rows are still rendered on main by `apps/cli/src/tui/components/chat-entry.tsx` case "team", which puts a long `<text selectable content={entry.text}>` inside a `<box flexDirection="row">` with no width/flexGrow/flexShrink and no `wrapMode`; in that layout the text node collapses toward its min-content width (longest word), which is exactly the one-word-per-line screenshot. No commit touching that renderer exists since the 2026-07-09 report.
notes: Owned by @cline/cli TUI rendering. Suspect the `flexDirection="row"` bullet+text pattern in chat-entry.tsx needs `flexGrow={1}`/explicit `wrapMode="word"` on the text child; the same pattern is used by the error/status rows so a shared fix is possible.

title: Cline hangs completely after skipping a command execution, requires VS Code restart
author: stefanCCS
evidence: The reporter himself flags #12079 ("Command execution shows 'skipped' in Cline terminal and hangs on 'thinking'", open, filed 2026-07-05) as the same bug, and the "Skipped" label is just the fall-through status in `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/CommandOutputRow.tsx` (`CommandStatusMap.skipped`) for a command row that never reached completed — i.e. a stuck command lifecycle, not a user action. On main the whole terminal stack was replaced by 12703bf40 (#11972, 2026-07-14, OSC 633 parser/exit codes/timeouts) after this report, and contributor @dominiccooney could not reproduce on 4.0.7 or nightly.
notes: Fold into #12079 and carry the extra data points there (two reporters state no Skip was ever clicked, so the trigger is runtime-side, and only an extension-host restart recovers). The underlying #12079 is still open and does need attention.

title: GLM 5.2 produces malformed file paths / search blocks when routed through Cline Pass, but works correctly via OpenRouter
author: ChrisTentum
evidence: All three quoted errors come from the legacy edit stack: `"Document not initialized"` exists only at `origin/legacy-extension:apps/vscode/src/integrations/editor/FileEditProvider.ts:42` and has no match anywhere on main, and `replace_in_file`/`write_to_file` survive on main only as legacy aliases mapped to the SDK `editor` tool (`sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/orchestration/runtime-builder.ts:94`). `apps/vscode/src/integrations/editor/` on main contains only `EditPreview.ts` and `CommentReviewController.ts` — FileEditProvider is gone.

Worth a retest on the SDK build against the `editor` tool before closing.

title: Cline 4.0.7 isn't loading on VS Codium
author: atiq-cs
evidence: The reporter's own log shows `[Cline] extension activated in 151ms` and `ExtensionService#_doActivateExtension saoudrizwan.claude-dev` succeeding, so activation is fine and the failure is view resolution. On main the sidebar view is registered unconditionally at `apps/vscode/src/extension.ts:119` (`vscode.window.registerWebviewViewProvider(VscodeWebviewProvider.SIDEBAR_ID, ...)`, id `claude-dev.SidebarProvider`), and `apps/vscode/package.json` declares `engines.vscode: ^1.101.0` with `activationEvents: [onLanguage, onUri, onStartupFinished]`, all satisfied by the reporter's VS Codium 1.112. Nothing in the log or the code identifies the defect.
notes: Reporter states it is workspace-dependent ("loads in some projects, not most others") and that it eventually self-recovered after `Cline: Focus on view`. Needs a VS Codium repro with a specific workspace plus the webview/renderer log, not just the extension-host log. Also a churn-risk report worth a human reply.

title: Using Meta MuseSpark v1.1,  Cline returns error "Cline uses complex prompts..."
author: philfung
evidence: The quoted string is the old 3.x `mistake_limit_reached` copy and does not exist anywhere on main (`rg "iterative task execution"` → no matches; the only surviving "Cline uses complex prompts" text is the static provider-settings warning in `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/settings/providers/OpenAICompatible.tsx:603`). On main the same condition renders "Cline ran into N errors in a row and stopped the task" from `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-interaction-coordinator.ts` `handleConsecutiveMistakeLimitReached`. The trigger is unchanged though: a model that can't emit valid tool calls trips `MistakeTracker` in `sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/safety/mistake-tracker.ts`.
notes: #5915 is the canonical thread for this and is already labeled "Model Quality". The bug template itself requires reproducibility on Claude Sonnet 4.5 (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml:8); a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint that cannot do native tool calls is out of that bar.

title: CLI ask_question() just spins
author: gregbacchus
evidence: Every link in the chain still exists on main and looks wired: `ask_question` is registered by `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.ts:927` and is `enableAskQuestion: true` in both the act and plan presets (`sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/presets.ts:33,51`); the executor is passed from `apps/cli/src/runtime/interactive/session-runtime.ts:158` through `askQuestionRef`, set by `apps/cli/src/tui/hooks/use-runtime-dialog-bridge.tsx` `setAskQuestion`, and rendered by `apps/cli/src/tui/views/chat-view.tsx` via `InlineToolResponse`. `askQuestion` is also a valid hub-routed executor (`sdk/packages/shared/src/hub.ts:609`). No fix commit since 3.0.39 (main is 3.0.46).
notes: Second reporter (@hajilok) confirms. Prime suspect is the hub tool-capability round trip for `askQuestion` (`sdk/packages/core/src/hub/server/hub-client-contributions.ts` toolExecutor contributions) rather than the TUI bridge, since the local-runtime path resolves the ref synchronously.

title: Cline: Queued prompt Is lost after using "Start New Task" and reopening the original task.
author: kirtirajsinh-dot
evidence: The queue is pure in-memory session state: `pendingPrompts: PendingPrompt[]` is a field on `ActiveSession` (`sdk/packages/core/src/types/session.ts:35`) managed by `sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/turn-queue/pending-prompt-service.ts`, and there is no persistence of it anywhere in the storage layer. The VS Code side only ever reads it live off the active session (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts:1958` calls `activeSession.sdkHost.pendingPrompts("list", ...)`), so "Start New Task" disposing the session drops the queue and reopening from history rehydrates messages but not queued prompts.
notes: Owned by @cline/core (turn-queue). Needs a product decision: persist `pendingPrompts` alongside the session record, or warn/flush the queue when a task is switched away from. QA-filed with a video, and the same loss will hit any surface that disposes a session.

title: Cline gets stuck at step 8 (verification) during Phase 4 implementation and does not proceed
author: mohitbashyal
evidence: "Step 8" is the reporter's own blueprint numbering, not a Cline concept; the only concrete detail is that Cline hung while running syntax checks and "starting the dev server". On main a foreground command that never exits is expected to block the turn until the user detaches — `apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.ts` awaits `process` and exposes `applyDetach`, surfaced as the "Proceed While Running" button (`apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/chat-view/shared/buttonConfig.ts:82,197`). No logs, no session id, no error text to distinguish that from the genuine hang in #12079.

title: Typed prompt intermittently lost when switching from Act mode to Plan mode before sending
author: MDReptile
