title: GPT 5.5 not working -  'function_call' was provided without its required 'reasoning' item
author: ChristofferOhlsen
evidence: `@cline/llms` cannot round-trip OpenAI Responses-API reasoning items. `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/vendors/openai.ts` builds the model with `provider.responses(modelId)`, and `shouldIncludeReasoningHistory` (`ai-sdk.ts:254`) keeps reasoning in history for openai-native, but `toAiSdkMessages` (`ai-sdk.ts:288-312`) only re-attaches `providerOptions.anthropic.{signature,redactedData}` on reasoning parts and only `providerOptions.google.thoughtSignature` on tool-call parts — nothing captures or replays `openai.itemId` / `reasoningEncryptedContent`. In `@ai-sdk/openai@3.0.84` that path falls into the `else` branch and warns "Non-OpenAI reasoning parts are not supported. Skipping reasoning part", so the function_call is sent while its paired `rs_...` item is dropped, which is exactly the 400 the reporter got.
notes: Owned by @cline/llms. Fix is to capture the openai reasoning item id / encrypted content off `part.providerMetadata.openai` in `emitAiSdkEvents` and replay it as `providerOptions.openai` in `toAiSdkMessages`. Blocks gpt-5.5 on the native OpenAI provider once a tool call is in history.

title: Repeated command execution and task continuation after stop in Git review task
author: infopg
evidence: The "kept going after I stopped it" half is visible on main: `apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.ts:366` sets `applyAbort = () => process.continue()`, and `apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/terminal/VscodeTerminalManager.ts:27` documents that `continue()` "resolves promise and stops event emission" — it explicitly does not terminate the command. The "repeated identical commands" half also has a real gap: `sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/safety/loop-detection.ts` only tracks `lastToolName`/`lastToolSignature`, so a repeating *cycle* of different git commands (fetch → diff --stat → diff -- file → branch → fetch …) never trips the consecutive-identical detector.
notes: Contributor @CoderSufiyan independently traced the same `process.continue()` gap on main. Safety-relevant: @fastfret888 reports commands (builds, deploys) firing after "Task Completed". Two separable fixes — kill the foreground process on abort, and extend loop detection beyond strictly-consecutive identical calls.

title: `reasoning-delta` stream parts are silently dropped in `@cline/llms` (wrong field name: `part.reasoning` instead of `part.delta`)

title: Cline: Thinking state does not disappear in chat after switching from Act Mode to Plan Mode during task execution.
author: kirtirajsinh-dot

author: leesilverman

Reporter has a live AIP environment and offered to validate. Note the Bedrock provider manifest in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/providers.generated.ts` does declare `tools`, so a provider-level fallback may be a simpler lever than base-model resolution.

title: VSCode/Cline/GPT5.4(high) are constantly running near 1M context size, sometimes going over.

title: Feature Request: Allow independently collapsing the command/script section within an API Request block (separate from the output section)

title: Checkpoint restore fails with "No checkpoint found at or before run N" after internal continuations
author: aeltorio
evidence: The reporter's root-cause analysis holds on `main`. `createCheckpointHooks` in `sdk/packages/core/src/hooks/checkpoint-hooks.ts` does `beforeRun: async ({snapshot}) => { ...; runCount += 1; }` with no distinction between a user turn and an internal continuation, and `sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts` routes both `run()` and `continue()` through the same private `execute()`, which calls `callBeforeRunHooks()` unconditionally. Meanwhile `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-checkpoints.ts` computes its run number by counting `isVisibleCheckpointUserMessage` entries (`say === "task"` / `"user_feedback"`), so the two counters diverge permanently after the first continuation and `checkpoint-restore.ts` then throws `No checkpoint found at or before run N in session ...`.
notes: PR #12387 is OPEN and unmerged at tip e4091c368 despite two commenters thanking the author for "the fix" — needs maintainer review. Affects both VS Code and CLI since the counter lives in `@cline/core`.

title: Cline tries to access LiteLLM routes blocked by default
author: Panossa
evidence: Confirmed on `main`, and the JetBrains label is indeed irrelevant since the code is shared. `fetchLiteLlmPrivateModels` in `sdk/packages/core/src/services/llms/provider-defaults.ts` builds its candidate list solely from `buildLiteLlmModelInfoUrls` = `[${baseUrl}/v1/model/info, ${baseUrl}/model/info]`, tries each with `x-litellm-api-key` then `Authorization`, and if all four attempts fail throws `LiteLLM model refresh failed. title: Cline: Task content is cleared after reopening an interrupted task
author: kirtirajsinh-dot
evidence: Both reported symptoms map to live code on main: `clearTask()` in `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-control-coordinator.ts` rejects any outstanding interaction with the literal string `"Task cleared"` (`this.options.interactions.clearPending("Task cleared")`), and `showTaskWithId()` in the same file installs an empty task proxy and logs `No messages found for task` when `taskHistory.getClineMessages(taskId)` returns nothing, which renders a blank chat. `cancelTask()` in that file aborts the SDK session and appends a `resume_task` ask but does not flush pending message persistence first, so an interrupt/reopen race is plausible.

title: CLI command execution hangs on background processes (bash & + wait pattern)
author: mrcoffeebreak
evidence: Both execution paths on main can stall on a backgrounded child. In `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts`, `spawnAndCollect()` only settles on `child.on("close")` (there is no `exit` handler), and `close` waits for every inherited stdio pipe to close, so a `&`-detached server holding stdout defers resolution to the timeout. In the foreground/`integrated` terminal path, `apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.ts` sets `VSCODE_FOREGROUND_RUN_COMMANDS_TIMEOUT_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000` (one hour), which is indistinguishable from an indefinite hang; the only escape is the "Proceed While Running" detach handle registered in `executeForeground()`.
notes: Owned jointly by @cline/core (`extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts` close-vs-exit) and apps/vscode (`vscode-run-commands-tool.ts` foreground timeout). The reporter's root-cause analysis is essentially correct.

title: Cline can not powershell7
author: Fireqtian
evidence: Two concrete defects on main match the report. First, `getAvailableTerminalProfiles()` in `apps/vscode/src/utils/shell.ts` hardcodes the PowerShell 7 profile path to `SHELL_PATHS.POWERSHELL_7` = `C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe`, even though the same file already has `getWindowsPwshInstallPaths()` which probes `ProgramW6432`, Program Files 6/7 and the Store install; and `getWindowsShellFromVSCode()` falls back to `SHELL_PATHS.POWERSHELL_LEGACY` whenever the named profile is missing from `terminal.integrated.profiles.windows`. Second, the garbling is explained by `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts:91`, where `createRollingCollector` decodes all child output with `new StringDecoder("utf8")` — Windows PowerShell 5.1 on a zh-CN console emits GBK, which becomes mojibake. Background Exec routes through this collector via `createShellExecutor` in `apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.ts`.
notes: Note #12331 (2026-07-18, `fix(vscode): shell mismatch between prompt, execution, and user configuration on Windows`) shipped in v4.0.10 (tagged 2026-07-20), so the reporter already has it; the hardcoded pwsh path and the UTF-8-only output decoder are the remaining gaps.

title: 🔒 Security: MCP Integration Leaks Complete process.env to MCP Servers
author: Correctover
evidence: The finding holds on main, at a slightly different location than cited: `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/mcp/client.ts` spawns stdio MCP servers with `env: { ...process.env, ...(transport.env ?? {}) }` (in `spawnProcess()`, around the `spawn(transport.command, ...)` call). By contrast the VS Code host does the safe thing — `apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts` builds its `StdioClientTransport` with `env: { ...getDefaultEnvironment(), ...(expandedConfig.env || {}) }`. So the CLI/hub/desktop hosts that use `@cline/core`'s own MCP client hand the full parent environment to every stdio MCP server, while the VS Code path does not.
notes: Owned by @cline/core. Real inconsistency worth closing (align `extensions/mcp/client.ts` with the MCP SDK's `getDefaultEnvironment()` allowlist), though impact is limited to servers the user explicitly configured locally. The report is padded with self-promotion (vendor site, Zenodo DOI, @-pings of unrelated users) — judge the code claim, not the packaging.

title: Groq provider always sends ~42k tokens on fresh workspace, causing 413 "Request too large"
author: seays-0715
evidence: The arithmetic points at Groq's TPM accounting, not a Cline bug. Groq counts `input + max_completion_tokens` against TPM, and `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/gateway.ts:22` sets `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 32_000`, which `resolveGatewayRequestMaxTokens()` uses whenever the caller does not request an explicit `maxTokens`. 42,451 − 32,000 ≈ 10.4k, which matches Cline's baseline prompt: `sdk/packages/shared/src/prompt/system.ts` is ~6.6 KB and `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.ts` ~30 KB of tool schemas. The catalog entry `openai/gpt-oss-20b` under `groq` in `catalog.generated.ts` declares `contextWindow: 131072`, so nothing is misconfigured — the account's 8,000 TPM tier simply cannot fit an agentic system prompt plus a 32k output reservation.
notes: Answerable without a maintainer: Cline is not sending 42k of content. If the team wants a follow-up, the discussable knob is lowering `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` or deriving it from the model's remaining context for low-TPM tiers.

title: Cline: Cline completes the task eventhough user logs out in middle of the ongoing task
author: RajatNagoria

The only other auth-change hook, `apps/vscode/src/core/controller/account/authStateChanged.ts`, just writes `userInfo` to global state. Nothing aborts an in-flight run on logout.
notes: Owned by apps/vscode. Needs a product decision as much as a fix: BYOK users are not signed in at all, so the abort should probably be conditional on the active provider being Cline-managed (`cline`/`cline-pass`) rather than on sign-in state generally.

title: Cline: Reset chat fails with "Could not map edited message to persisted conversation history" Error.
author: kirtirajsinh-dot
evidence: The exact error string is thrown on main by `SdkController.editMessageAndRegenerate()` in `apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts`, when `findSdkUserMessageIndexByOrdinal(sdkMessages, userOrdinal)` returns -1. That helper (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-user-message-mapping.ts`) counts visible user turns positionally and skips messages it classifies as synthetic via `isSyntheticSdkUserMessage`/`extractSdkUserText`, while the ordinal on the other side is computed by filtering `clineMessages` for `say === "task" || say === "user_feedback"`. The mapping is acknowledged as fragile in `sdk-user-message-mapping.test.ts`, which notes that a mis-classified synthetic prompt makes "every later edit/regenerate ordinal shift by one". Nothing has changed in either file since the report (latest touches are #12552 and #12558, unrelated).
notes: Owned by apps/vscode. Positional ordinal mapping between UI `ClineMessage`s and persisted SDK messages is the weak point; a stable id stamped on both sides would remove the whole class of failure.

title: Gemini adapter turns nested MCP arrays into STRING and drops their schema
author: veerawatS
evidence: The `array: "STRING"` mapping the reporter identifies exists only on the retired branch: `git grep -n 'STRING' origin/legacy-extension -- apps/vscode/src` finds the type table in `apps/vscode/src/core/prompts/system-prompt/spec.ts` (`string: "STRING"`, `array: "STRING"`, line ~236), and that whole `system-prompt/` tree is gone on main (`apps/vscode/src/core/prompts/` now contains only `responses.ts` and `__tests__`). On main, MCP tool schemas are forwarded verbatim: `createMcpTools()` in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/mcp/tools.ts` passes `descriptor.inputSchema` straight into `createTool`, and `toAiSdkTools()` in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts` wraps it with `jsonSchema(normalizeAiSdkToolInputSchema(...))`, which only ensures a top-level `type: "object"` and otherwise leaves `items`/nested `properties`/`required` untouched, letting the AI SDK's Google provider do the OpenAPI conversion.
notes: Excellent, precisely-diagnosed report — but against the 3.x extension that the A/B rollout still ships alongside 4.x under a 4.0.x version string. Worth replying with the fact that the hand-rolled type table is gone on main and asking them to retest on the SDK build; their suggested regression test (assert the Gemini wire declaration keeps `rules`/`steps` as arrays) would still be a good addition to `ai-sdk.tool-calls.test.ts`.

title: [Feature Request] 添加中文界面支持 / Add Chinese (Simplified) Language Support
author: Muss0504
evidence: No localization layer exists on main: searching `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src` for `i18n`, `useTranslation` or `react-intl` returns no matches, and UI strings are hardcoded English literals throughout the chat and settings components (e.g. "Edit and regenerate from here", "Reset Chat" in `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/UserMessage.tsx`). Adding zh-CN therefore means introducing an i18n framework plus extraction across the whole webview, not just a language pack.
notes: Large, cross-cutting change to `apps/vscode/webview-ui` (framework choice, string extraction, a language setting in the settings surface, and ongoing translation upkeep). Needs a product/maintainer decision before any code work; note the existence of the third-party `cline-chinese` fork as prior art.

title: fix(cli): openai-compatible provider ignores models.json contextWindow — resolveModelInfo ?? short-circuits on default   messageModelInfo
author: yangyuliufeng
evidence: The reporter's versions match tip of main exactly (`apps/cli/package.json` is 3.0.46, `sdk/packages/core/package.json` is 0.0.65) and both cited code sites are present verbatim: `resolveModelInfo()` in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/compat.ts` still reads `config.modelInfo ?? (config.modelId ? config.knownModels?.[config.modelId] : undefined) ?? {...}`, and `resolveRuntimeConfig()` in `sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts` still sets `const messageModelInfo = rest.messageModelInfo ?? { id: modelId, provider: providerId }`. The 115.2k figure is confirmed by `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context/compaction-shared.ts` (`DEFAULT_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS = 128_000`, `COMPACTION_TRIGGER_RATIO = 0.9` → 115,200) applied in `compaction.ts` when `resolveEffectiveMaxInputTokens` yields nothing.
notes: The `??` ordering defect in `resolveModelInfo` is real and still shadows registry data for `handler.getModel().info` (which is what the cost calculator reads — matching the $0.00 symptom). Caveat for whoever picks this up: the *compaction trigger* has partial mitigation already — `compaction.ts` reads `context.model.info` from `tryGetModelInfo()` in `sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/orchestration/session-runtime-orchestrator.ts`, which prefers `knownModels`, and `resolveProviderMaxInputTokens()` in `agentic-compaction.ts` falls back to `knownModels` (added in 10cb9bd97, #12142, 2026-07-09). So verify which of the two symptoms still reproduces before assuming one fix covers both.

title: Could not use latset Gemini models: "prefill model turn" is removed
author: Vectorial1024
evidence: Real forward-compat gap. `gemini-3.6-flash` and `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` are already in the `gemini` block of `sdk/packages/llms/src/catalog/catalog.generated.ts`, so users can select them on main, but nothing in the request pipeline prevents a trailing assistant turn: `toAiSdkMessages`/`formatMessagesForAiSdk` in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/ai-sdk.ts` and `sdk/packages/shared/src/llms/ai-sdk-format.ts` pass the conversation through as-is (they even emit an empty-content assistant turn rather than dropping it), and grepping for `prefill` across `sdk/packages/` returns no handling at all. Google's documented change (`Prefilling model turns is no longer supported`) therefore surfaces as the 400 `Requests ending with a model turn are not supported` the commenters pasted.
notes: Blocks #12474. Google states the change applies to all future Gemini releases, so this needs a general rule rather than a per-model patch.

title: Plugin stores skills in `~/.agents/skills` but reads from `~/.cline/skills/`
author: til2000
evidence: The title's claim is contradicted by main: both roots are scanned. `getSkillsDirectoriesForScan()` in `apps/vscode/src/core/storage/skill-directories.ts` returns the global pair `~/.cline/skills` and `~/.agents/skills`, and `resolveSkillsConfigSearchPaths()` in `sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts` appends `join(resolveClineDir(), SKILLS_CONFIG_DIRECTORY_NAME)` and `join(HOME_DIR, LEGACY_AGENT_SKILLS_CONFIG_DIR /* ".agents" */, SKILLS_CONFIG_DIRECTORY_NAME)`; `getGlobalMarketplaceSkillPaths()` in `sdk/packages/core/src/services/marketplace.ts` checks both too. Neither file has changed since well before 4.0.10 (`skill-directories.ts` last touched 2026-06-10; the `.agents` search path landed in 9f42aea85, #11103, 2026-05-28). The report has an empty repro template, so I cannot tell whether the complaint is non-discovery or a wrong path being *displayed*.
notes: Answerable by an agent: ask whether the skills under `~/.agents/skills` failed to appear in the skills list at all, or merely showed a `~/.cline/skills/...` path in the transcript, and for the exact install command used.

title: Global Cline rules are not loaded in new VS Code sessions on macOS
author: olhado
evidence: Two of the reporter's three locations are legitimately in scope on main and one is not. `resolveRulesConfigSearchPaths()` in `sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts` returns the workspace `AGENTS.md`, workspace `.clinerules`, workspace `.cline/rules`, `resolveGlobalAgentsRulesPath()` (`~/.agents/AGENTS.md`), `join(resolveClineDir(), RULES_CONFIG_DIRECTORY_NAME)` (`~/.cline/rules`) and `resolveDocumentsExtensionPath("Rules")` (`~/Documents/Cline/Rules`) — so `~/.cline/rules/default-rules.md` and `~/Documents/Cline/Rules/default-rules.md` should both load, while a bare `~/.clinerules` home file is not a supported location at all. On the VS Code side `ensureRulesDirectoryExists()` in `apps/vscode/src/core/storage/disk.ts` resolves the Documents root via `getDocumentsPath()`, and rules are gated by per-rule enable/disable toggles synchronized in `apps/vscode/src/core/context/instructions/user-instructions/rule-helpers.ts`.
notes: Reporter says it started after an upgrade, which fits a toggle-state migration regression more than a path regression. Worth checking whether newly discovered global rules default to enabled after a version bump.

title: Cline: Cline initiates task creation despite user being logged out
author: RajatNagoria
evidence: There is no auth pre-flight before a task starts on main: the only `getAuthToken()` call in `apps/vscode/src/sdk` is in `account-service.ts` (balance/usage fetching), and neither the task-start path in `apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts` nor `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-control-coordinator.ts` consults auth state before creating a session — the failure only surfaces later as a provider `Unauthorized`. The cross-IDE half of the repro is also unguarded: `apps/vscode/src/core/controller/account/authStateChanged.ts` merely writes `userInfo` into global state, so one IDE completing the browser auth does not reconcile the other's view.
notes: Filed by Cline QA against nightly 4.0.1784896810. Needs a product call — BYOK users are legitimately never signed in, so any gate has to key off the selected provider being Cline-managed, not off sign-in state alone.

title: Cline defers devlog/logging actions until end of task instead of executing them in real-time after each milestone
author: Allenwavekwan
evidence: This is model-adherence behavior, not a code defect. The user's `.clinerules` file is loaded and injected as instructions (`resolveRulesConfigSearchPaths` in `sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts` includes the workspace `.clinerules`), and nothing in the runtime reorders or batches a model's tool calls — `run_commands` simply accepts a list, and `buildRunCommandsDescription()` in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/definitions.ts` explicitly encourages sequencing multiple commands in one call, which is the opposite of what this rule wants. There is no scheduler in `sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts` that could defer the echoes; the model chose to batch them.
notes: If the team wants to act on the underlying want, the right shape is a hook (`@cline/shared` hook engine) or a post-tool-use plugin that appends the devlog line deterministically, rather than relying on a prompt rule the model can batch away. Answerable without a maintainer.

title: it is impossible to remove image from chat
author: Wadkan
evidence: Visible in code on main. `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/UserMessage.tsx` renders only a `<textarea>` bound to `editedText` while `isEditing`, and the `<Thumbnails ... />` block is explicitly gated on `!isEditing`, so attachments are hidden (and un-removable) in edit mode. `handleSave()` then unconditionally resends the originals: `EditMessageAndRegenerateRequest.create({ messageTs, text: editedText, images: images ?? [], files: files ?? [], restoreWorkspace })`. There is no code path by which editing a message can drop an image, which matches the reporter's "only the text can be modified".
notes: Owned by `apps/vscode/webview-ui`. Fix is contained: render removable `Thumbnails` inside the edit branch of `UserMessage.tsx` and pass the pruned arrays into `EditMessageAndRegenerateRequest`. The secondary complaint (a non-multimodal OpenRouter model 404s on image input) would be worth a capability pre-check, since `catalog.generated.ts` already carries an `images` capability flag per model.

title: API Configuration: oLMX를 ollama/lm studio처럼 등록 가능하도록 추가
author: rAzorheAd777
evidence: The reporter means oMLX (github.com/jundot/omlx), a macOS/Apple-Silicon MLX inference server that is an OpenAI-compatible drop-in on http://localhost:8000/v1; `rg -i olmx` and a search of `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/provider-ids.generated.ts` show no oMLX/omlx provider id on main. Local-server presets like the ones requested do exist as hand-authored entries in `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtins.ts` (`id: "ollama"` at ~L867 and `id: "lmstudio"`, family `openai-compatible`, `defaults.baseUrl: http://localhost:1234/v1`), so adding oMLX is a small addition there plus the surfaced list in `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/settings/providers/providerSettingsRegistry.ts`. A workaround already exists on main: the generic OpenAI Compatible provider (`"openai"` in `CUSTOM_PROVIDER_SETTINGS_IDS`, UI in `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/settings/providers/OpenAICompatible.tsx`) accepts an arbitrary base URL.
notes: Owned by @cline/llms (`sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtins.ts`). Agent-fixable: one builtin entry modeled on `lmstudio` (family `openai-compatible`, baseUrl `http://localhost:8000/v1`, modelsSourceUrl `http://localhost:8000/v1/models`; oMLX also exposes `/v1/messages`). Until then users can point the existing OpenAI Compatible provider at oMLX, so it is answerable without maintainer input.
